import AlgebraicJacobian.Genus

/-! # The Jacobian of a smooth proper curve

The Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve over a field, equipped with
its structure as an abelian variety.

## Status

The Jacobian is defined uniformly as the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness
(`JacobianWitness`) for the curve `C`; the four protected instances on `Jacobian C` all
project from the witness directly.

The construction is **uniform in the genus**: the witness is the Picard identity
component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` (`picardJacobianWitness`), an abelian variety of dimension
`genus C` built by the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*` +
`AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.*`). There is **no** genus `= 0` / genus `> 0` split: when
`genus C = 0` the tangent space `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
falls out automatically. The former separate `genusZeroWitness` lane (with its
`RigidityKbar` / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery) was a
pre-FGA local optimisation and has been removed.

This file contains exactly ONE `sorry`-bodied mathematical declaration,
`picardJacobianWitness`, whose closure is the FGA construction of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` as an
abelian variety with its Albanese universal property.

  "Curve and scheme base objects" \
  "Sorry-free. Geometric connectedness and integrality of curve sections, base change of the curve along a field extension, standard-smooth relative dimension, finite Galois quotients and their affine charts, and stable affine covers. Modules: RiemannRoch/CurveBaseChange, Picard/GeometricallyConnectedSection, Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient, Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotientAffine, Picard/GaloisQuotientGlue, Picard/StableAffineCover, Albanese/StandardSmoothDimension, Albanese/SmoothPrimeRegularity."
add AJC.substrate.sheaves AJC.substrate done \
  "Quasi-coherent sheaves on schemes" \
  "Sorry-free. The tilde construction and its sections, restriction to basic opens, the over-category equivalence for sheaves on an open, conservativity of a module cover, exactness of tilde, structure-sheaf module objects over the base field, and quasi-coherence of pullbacks. Modules: Cohomology/QcohTildeSections, Cohomology/QcohRestrictBasicOpen, Cohomology/TildeExactness, Cohomology/ModulesCoverConservativity, Cohomology/SheafCompose, Cohomology/StructureSheafAb, Cohomology/StructureSheafModuleK, Cohomology/PullbackQuasicoherent, Picard/SheafOverEquivalence."
add AJC.substrate.relspec AJC.substrate done \
  "Relative Spec, projective morphisms, and section rings" \
  "Sorry-free. The relative spectrum of a quasi-coherent algebra, projective space and projective morphisms over a base, the universal property of the section ring, and localisation of invertible sections with its graded bridge. Modules: Picard/RelativeSpec, Picard/ProjectiveSpace, Picard/ProjectiveMorphism, Picard/SectionRingUniversal, Picard/InvertibleSectionLocalization, Picard/InvertibleGrBridge."
add AJC.substrate.descent AJC.substrate done \
  "Gluing and descent" \
  "Sorry-free. Gluing schemes and quasi-coherent data along an open cover, Zariski-local representability descent, and semilinear (Galois) descent for modules and algebras. Modules: Picard/GlueDescent, Picard/ZariskiDescentRepresentability, Picard/GaloisDescent/SemilinearModules, Picard/GaloisDescent/SemilinearAlgebras."
add AJC.substrate.tangent AJC.substrate done \
  "Dual numbers and tangent spaces" \
  "Sorry-free. Units of the dual numbers, scheme-valued points over k[eps], the identity-section tangent vector, the stalk-algebra description of the tangent space, and the dual-number cocycle presentation used for the Pic^0 tangent space. Modules: Picard/DualNumberUnits, Picard/TangentSpaceDualNumbers, Picard/TangentSpaceSchemePoints, Picard/TangentSpaceIdentitySection, Picard/TangentSpaceStalkAlgebra, Picard/Pic0DualNumberCocycle, Picard/Pic0TangentSpace."
add AJC.substrate.rigidity AJC.substrate done \
  "Rigidity lemma" \
  "Sorry-free. Mumford's rigidity lemma in Form I and the consequence that a pointed morphism of group schemes is a homomorphism, in hypotheses weaker than Milne I.1.2. Module: RigidityLemma."
add AJC.substrate.genus AJC.substrate done \
  "Genus and the Abel--Jacobi interface" \
  "Sorry-free. The genus of a smooth proper curve as dim_k H^1(C, O_C) together with the Abel--Jacobi interface consumed by the final witness. Modules: Genus, AbelJacobi."

echo "== AJC.cech =="
add AJC.cech.engine AJC.cech done \
  "Combinatorial and section Cech complexes" \
  "Sorry-free. The alternating coface complex of a presheaf, its free resolution, the section Cech complex of a finite affine cover, the contracting homotopy in degree zero, positive degree, and the isolated degree-one identity, and coboundary splitting. Modules: Cohomology/PresheafCech, Cohomology/FreePresheafComplex, Cohomology/CechSectionComplex, Cohomology/CechSectionContractibility, Cohomology/CechSectionContractibilityCore, Cohomology/CechSectionContractibilityOne, Cohomology/CechSectionContractibilitySucc, Cohomology/CechCoboundarySplitting."
add AJC.cech.identification AJC.cech done \
  "Section-complex identification" \
  "Sorry-free. Identification of the section Cech complex with the evaluated complex, through the base, leg, and top comparison stages and the augmentation comparison. Modules: Cohomology/CechSectionIdentification, Cohomology/CechSectionIdentificationBase, Cohomology/CechSectionIdentificationLeg, Cohomology/CechSectionIdentificationLegAux, Cohomology/CechSectionIdentificationLegMid1, Cohomology/CechSectionIdentificationLegMid2, Cohomology/CechSectionIdentificationLegTop, Cohomology/CechSectionAugmentationComparison."
add AJC.cech.acyclic AJC.cech done \
  "Affine acyclicity and acyclic resolutions" \
  "Sorry-free. Serre vanishing on affines, termwise acyclicity of the Cech complex, the generic exact-augmentation lemmas that compute cohomology from an acyclic resolution, and the augmented Cech resolution. Modules: Cohomology/AffineSerreVanishing, Cohomology/CechAcyclic, Cohomology/CechTermAcyclic, Cohomology/AcyclicResolution, Cohomology/CechAugmentedResolution."
add AJC.cech.pushpull AJC.cech done \
  "Higher direct images and pushPull functoriality" \
  "Sorry-free. Higher direct images as derived pushforward, their presheaf model, acyclicity of pushforward along an affine morphism, the essential image of affine pushPull, and pushforward along an open immersion. Modules: Cohomology/HigherDirectImage, Cohomology/HigherDirectImagePresheaf, Cohomology/AffinePushPullEssImage, Cohomology/OpenImmersionPushforward."
add AJC.cech.mayervietoris AJC.cech done \
  "Mayer--Vietoris for a two-element cover" \
  "Sorry-free. The Mayer--Vietoris sequence in the (0,1) slice for a two-element affine cover, and its cover-level packaging. Modules: Cohomology/MayerVietorisCore, Cohomology/MayerVietorisCover."
add AJC.cech.main AJC.cech done \
  "cech_computes_higherDirectImage" \
  "Sorry-free and unconditional (no enough-injectives appeal). For a separated quasi-compact morphism, a quasi-coherent sheaf, and a finite affine open cover, the cohomology of the relative Cech complex computes R^i f_*. Modules: Cohomology/AbsoluteCohomology, Cohomology/CechToCohomology, Cohomology/CechBridge, Cohomology/CechToHigherDirectImage."

echo "== AJC.grquot =="
add AJC.grquot.cells AJC.grquot done \
  "Grassmannian cells, charts, and representability" \
  "Sorry-free. The affine cell charts of the relative Grassmannian, their GL_d cocycle gluing, the Zariski sheaf condition, and the H^0 representability theorem Grassmannian.represents. Modules: Picard/GrassmannianCells, Picard/GrassmannianZariskiSheaf, Picard/GrassmannianRepresentability, Picard/GrassmannianQuot."
add AJC.grquot.graded AJC.grquot done \
  "Section graded ring and module" \
  "Sorry-free. The graded ring of sections of the Serre twists, the associated graded module of a quasi-coherent sheaf, and finiteness of its graded pieces. Modules: Picard/SectionGradedRing, Picard/GradedPiecesFinite, Picard/SerreTwist, Picard/SerreTwistSections."
add AJC.grquot.hilbertserre AJC.grquot done \
  "Graded Hilbert--Serre algebra and the Hilbert polynomial" \
  "Sorry-free. The Hilbert--Serre theorem for a finitely generated graded module over a polynomial ring and the resulting Hilbert polynomial with its uniqueness and specification API. Modules: Picard/GradedHilbertSerre, Picard/HilbertPolynomial."
add AJC.grquot.flattening AJC.grquot done \
  "Flattening stratification" \
  "Sorry-free. The entry-ideal stratification of a two-term presentation, its universal property, the flat-kernel base, and schematic support. Modules: Picard/FlatteningStratification, Picard/FlatteningStratificationUniversal, Picard/EntryIdeal, Picard/EntryIdealStratum, Picard/FlatKernelBase, Picard/SchematicSupport, Picard/TwoTermFiniteFree."
add AJC.grquot.genericflatness AJC.grquot done \
  "Generic flatness and finite presentation" \
  "Sorry-free. Geometric generic flatness for a finite-type morphism, stability of finite presentation under pullback, and the finite-presentation functor. Modules: Picard/GenericFlatnessGeometric, Picard/PullbackFinitePresentation, Picard/FinitePresentationFunctor."

echo "== AJC.linebundle =="
add AJC.linebundle.coherence AJC.linebundle done \
  "Line-bundle coherence" \
  "Sorry-free. Coherence and local freeness of invertible sheaves on a scheme, and the two-term finite free presentations they admit. Module: Picard/LineBundleCoherence."
add AJC.linebundle.pullback AJC.linebundle done \
  "Line-bundle pullback and the section formula" \
  "Sorry-free. Pullback of line bundles along a morphism, functoriality, and the tensor section formula. Modules: Picard/LineBundlePullback, Picard/TensorSectionFormula."
add AJC.linebundle.tensor AJC.linebundle done \
  "Tensor comparison substrate" \
  "Sorry-free. The stalk-tensor comparison, the presheaf internal hom, and the tensor-object substrate on which the comparison isomorphisms are built. Modules: Picard/TensorObjSubstrate, Picard/TensorObjSubstrate/StalkTensor, Picard/TensorObjSubstrate/PresheafInternalHom."
add AJC.linebundle.dual AJC.linebundle done \
  "Dual comparison and the terminal inverse" \
  "Sorry-free. The slice-dual transport isomorphism, presheaf dual pullback with its unit, composition and naturality, trivialisation restriction compatibility, and the terminal comparison inverse giving Pic^sharp its group law. Modules: Picard/TensorObjInverse, Picard/TensorObjSubstrate/DualInverse and its PresheafDualPullback, PresheafDualUnitPullback, PresheafDualPullbackComposition, PresheafDualPullbackNatural, SliceTransport and TrivialisationRestrict components."
add AJC.linebundle.picgroup AJC.linebundle done \
  "Relative Picard functor and its group law" \
  "Sorry-free. The relative Picard functor of a curve over a base, its rigidified variant, and the abelian-group structure supplied by the comparison isomorphisms. Modules: Picard/RelPicFunctor, Picard/RigidifiedPic."

echo "== AJC.rr =="
add AJC.rr.adelic AJC.rr done \
  "Adelic Riemann--Roch and cohomological finiteness" \
  "Sorry-free. The adelic model of H^0 and H^1 for a smooth proper curve: a nonconstant map to P^1, its finiteness, the P^1 base case and chart data, the adelic cokernel, the Euler-characteristic ledger, and unconditional finiteness of the genus. Modules: RiemannRoch/CohomologyKit and the RiemannRoch/Adelic package (Substrate, NonconstantToP1, FiniteMapToP1, FinitenessP1, P1BaseCase, P1ChartData, Cokernel, ChiLedger, CechAcyclicInstance, CechComparisonGate, GateInstances, GenusFiniteness, GenusUnconditional)."
add AJC.rr.principal AJC.rr pending \
  "Principal divisors have degree zero" \
  "The single remaining in-tree Riemann--Roch obligation: deg(div f) = 0 for a nonzero rational function on a smooth proper curve, in RiemannRoch/WeilDivisor. The finite-map and pullback-degree gates are stated; the divisor-degree and divisor-functor substrate (Picard/DivDegree, Picard/DivFunctorDef) is otherwise sorry-free."

echo "== AJC.albanese =="
add AJC.albanese.ab AJC.albanese done \
  "Auslander--Buchsbaum and the coheight bridge" \
  "Sorry-free. The Auslander--Buchsbaum formula and the coheight bridge relating codimension to depth, together with pole purity; these feed the codimension-one extension of rational maps. Modules: Albanese/AuslanderBuchsbaum, Albanese/CoheightBridge, Albanese/PolePurity."
add AJC.albanese.rationalmaps AJC.albanese done \
  "Rational-map substrate" \
  "Sorry-free. Rational maps to a scheme through the function field, precomposition and products, the difference map of a rational map to a group scheme, the Milne III.3.3 substeps, and the Theorem 3.2 rational-map extension. Modules: Albanese/RationalMapFunctionField, Albanese/RationalMapPrecomp, Albanese/RationalMapProd, Albanese/DifferenceMap, Albanese/Milne33Substeps, Albanese/Thm32RationalMapExtension."

echo "== AJC.picrep =="
add AJC.picrep.rigidpushforward AJC.picrep done \
  "Rigidified pushforward engine" \
  "Sorry-free. The rigidified pushforward of a line bundle along the structure morphism, the P^1 engine and its transfer, finiteness of chart and P^1 sections, semicontinuity of h^0, faithfulness of the scalar endomorphisms, and section base change. Modules: Picard/RigidPushforward, Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Engine, Picard/RigidPushforwardTransfer, Picard/ChartSectionsFinite, Picard/P1SectionsFinite, Picard/SemicontinuityH0, Picard/ScalarEndFaithful, Picard/SectionBaseChange."
add AJC.picrep.quotbasechange AJC.picrep done \
  "Quot base change and support" \
  "Sorry-free. Flat base change for the Quot construction and base change of the support of a quotient; these are the inputs the Nitsure representability endgame consumes. Modules: Picard/QuotFlatBaseChange, Picard/QuotSupportBaseChange, and the quasi-coherent descent machinery of Picard/QuotScheme."

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Normalise the copyright header of every module in the AlgebraicJacobian library.

Rationale: 138 of 164 modules carried `Copyright (c) 2026 Christian Merten` /
`Authors: Christian Merten`, copied from the seed statement file
`references/challenge.lean`.  Christian Merten proposed the challenge; he did not
write this project's code, so the attribution is wrong.  The sibling project
Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild already settled on the header below; this
brings the two projects into line and also satisfies mathlib's
`linter.style.header` (which currently reports "Copyright too short!" and
"Copyright line should end with '. All rights reserved.'").

Run from the project root.  Prints one line per changed file.
"""
import os
import re
import sys

CANON = """/-
Copyright (c) 2026 The AlgebraicJacobian authors. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
-/"""

root = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "AlgebraicJacobian"
changed = added = 0

for dirpath, _, filenames in os.walk(root):
    for fn in sorted(filenames):
        if not fn.endswith(".lean"):
            continue
        path = os.path.join(dirpath, fn)
        text = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        m = re.match(r"/-\n(Copyright[^\n]*\n)(Released[^\n]*\n)?(Authors:[^\n]*\n)?-/", text)
        if m:
            if m.group(0) == CANON:
                continue
            text = CANON + text[m.end():]
            changed += 1
            print("header:", path)
        else:
            # No recognisable header block: prepend the canonical one.
            text = CANON + "\n" + text
            added += 1
            print("added: ", path)
        open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(text)

print(f"normalised {changed} headers, added {added}")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Replace a module's bare `import Mathlib` by the precise Mathlib imports it needs.
#
#   scripts/deumbrella.sh AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Foo.lean
#
# Procedure: probe with `scripts/min-imports.sh` (Mathlib's `#import_bumps`
# linter), rewrite the import block, then re-elaborate the file with
# `lake env lean`.  On any failure the original file is restored, so the tree is
# never left broken.  Prints one summary line:
#
#   OK    <file>  <n> precise imports (was: import Mathlib)
#   SKIP  <file>  <reason>
#   FAIL  <file>  <reason>   (original restored)
#
# A module only stops paying for the umbrella once NO module in its transitive
# project-import closure is bare, so convert DAG sources first.
set -uo pipefail

SRC=${1:?usage: deumbrella.sh <file.lean>}
HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
OUT=${AJC_DEUMBRELLA_OUT:-/tmp/ajc-minimports}
mkdir -p "$OUT"

grep -qx 'import Mathlib' "$SRC" || { echo "SKIP  $SRC  no bare import Mathlib"; exit 0; }

probe="$OUT/$(basename "$SRC" .lean).probe.txt"
bash "$HERE/min-imports.sh" "$SRC" "$OUT" > "$probe" 2>&1

grep -q '^STATUS ok' "$probe" || { echo "SKIP  $SRC  probe did not elaborate (see $probe)"; exit 0; }
grep -qx "UNNEEDED Mathlib" "$probe" || { echo "SKIP  $SRC  linter did not report Mathlib unneeded"; exit 0; }

bak="$SRC.deumbrella.bak"
cp "$SRC" "$bak"

python3 - "$SRC" "$probe" <<'PY'
import sys
src, probe = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
missing = [l.split(None, 1)[1].strip()
           for l in open(probe, encoding="utf-8") if l.startswith("MISSING ")]
mathlib = sorted(m for m in missing if m == "Mathlib" or m.startswith("Mathlib."))
other = [m for m in missing if m not in mathlib]

lines = open(src, encoding="utf-8").read().split("\n")
out, done = [], False
for l in lines:
    if l == "import Mathlib" and not done:
        out.extend(f"import {m}" for m in mathlib)
        out.extend(f"import {m}" for m in other)
        done = True
        continue
    out.append(l)
open(src, "w", encoding="utf-8").write("\n".join(out))
print(len(mathlib) + len(other))
PY

n=$(grep -c '^import Mathlib\.' "$SRC")

if lake env lean \
     -Dpp.unicode.fun=true \
     -DrelaxedAutoImplicit=false \
     -DmaxSynthPendingDepth=3 \
     -Dweak.linter.mathlibStandardSet=true \
     "$SRC" > "$OUT/$(basename "$SRC" .lean).verify.txt" 2>&1; then
  rm -f "$bak"
  echo "OK    $SRC  $n precise imports"
else
  mv "$bak" "$SRC"
  echo "FAIL  $SRC  verification failed, restored (see $OUT/$(basename "$SRC" .lean).verify.txt)"
fi

export const meta = {
  name: 'ajc-blueprint-cleanup',
  description: 'Make the AJC blueprint read as timeless mathematics: remove development-journal prose, split the two oversized chapters, fix dangling pins and false leanok',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Survey', detail: 'map journal prose, oversized chapters, dangling pins' },
    { title: 'Clean', detail: 'one agent per chapter group' },
    { title: 'Check', detail: 'graph sync + adversarial re-read' },
  ],
}

const ROOT = '/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon'
const PROJ = ROOT + '/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge'
const BP = PROJ + '/blueprint/src/chapters'

const RULES = `
PROJECT: ${PROJ} (Lean 4 + leanblueprint). Blueprint chapters: ${BP}.

BINDING HOUSE RULES — read ${ROOT}/.claude/skills/blueprint-conventions/SKILL.md IN FULL first.
The essentials you must enforce:
- The blueprint is TIMELESS MATHEMATICS, a standalone document. It is never a formalization
  journal. Delete on sight: "iter-NNN", "run NNNN", "Lane X", "STAGE n", "landed", "sorry-free",
  "we tried", "the current Lean file", "TODO", route comparisons, status/progress reports, dates,
  agent or session references, tier lists, and any sentence about the Lean development process.
  Lean implementation notes do NOT go in .tex — they belong on the hgraph node.
- Every \\begin{proof} must contain a COMPLETE rigorous mathematical proof. If a proof is long,
  SPLIT it: break the hard step out as its own \\label'ed lemma with \\uses, do not abbreviate.
  Never leave "clear", "standard", "omitted", "see [ref]" as the whole proof.
- One statement's worth per node. \\lean{Name} must name a Lean declaration that really exists.
  \\leanok on a proof means that proof is formalized and checked.
- \\source{slug:page-0001} anchors cite references/; do not paste source quotes into comments.

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
- You may edit ONLY files under ${PROJ}/blueprint/. Do NOT touch any .lean file, the lakefile,
  or anything under ${PROJ}/AlgebraicJacobian/ — a timed Lean build is running on this machine.
- Do NOT run \`lake\`, \`lean\`, or any Lean LSP tool. Grep/sed/python/Read/Edit/Write only.
- Never DELETE a mathematical statement or a proof to make prose "cleaner". You are removing
  journal narration and completing sketched proofs, not shrinking content. If a proof is a stub
  and you cannot honestly write the real argument, keep the statement, write the best complete
  argument you can, and if a genuine gap remains state it as an explicit named dependency
  (\\uses to a lemma node that is itself unproved) rather than hand-waving.
- Every claim you make about a Lean declaration must be grepped, not guessed.
`

phase('Survey')

const SURVEY = await agent(`${RULES}
Survey the whole blueprint and return a work plan. Report:
1. Every chapter file with its line count.
2. For each chapter, the count and 3 worst verbatim examples of development-journal prose
   (grep for: iter-, run 0, Lane , STAGE, landed, sorry-free, TODO, "we ", "our ", "currently",
   "at present", "for now", "note that the Lean", "the Lean file", "in this iteration",
   "Route A", "Route B", "Route C", "planner", "brick", "worksheet", dates like 2026-).
3. Chapters over 3000 lines and a proposed split into coherent mathematical sub-chapters
   (give the proposed new filenames and which \\label ranges move where), plus how content.tex
   must change.
4. Every \\begin{proof} whose body is under 3 lines or contains "clear"/"standard"/"omitted"/
   "similar"/"analogous"/"see " with no argument — file:line.
5. Every \\lean{X} whose X does not exist in ${PROJ}/AlgebraicJacobian (grep the tree).
6. Duplicate \\label declarations, and \\uses{L} for labels L that do not exist.
Be exhaustive and exact; the next agents execute from this.`, { schema: {
  type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
  required: ['chapters', 'oversized', 'dangling_pins', 'stub_proofs', 'label_problems'],
  properties: {
    chapters: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
      required: ['file', 'lines', 'journal_hits', 'worst_examples'],
      properties: { file: { type: 'string' }, lines: { type: 'integer' },
        journal_hits: { type: 'integer' }, worst_examples: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } } } } },
    oversized: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false,
      required: ['file', 'lines', 'proposed_split'],
      properties: { file: { type: 'string' }, lines: { type: 'integer' }, proposed_split: { type: 'string' } } } },
    dangling_pins: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    stub_proofs: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
    label_problems: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' } },
  },
} })

log(`survey: ${SURVEY.chapters.length} chapters, ${SURVEY.dangling_pins.length} dangling pins, ${SURVEY.stub_proofs.length} stub proofs`)

// Group chapters into batches of roughly equal journal-cleanup weight, worst first.
const ranked = [...SURVEY.chapters].sort((a, b) => (b.journal_hits || 0) - (a.journal_hits || 0))
const dirty = ranked.filter(c => (c.journal_hits || 0) > 0)
const BATCHES = []
const PER = 3
for (let i = 0; i < dirty.length; i += PER) BATCHES.push(dirty.slice(i, i + PER))

phase('Clean')

const cleaned = await pipeline(
  BATCHES,
  (batch, _b, i) => agent(`${RULES}
You own these blueprint chapters end to end. Rewrite each so it reads as timeless mathematics.

CHAPTERS (file — line count — journal hits — examples):
${batch.map(c => `- ${c.file} (${c.lines} lines, ${c.journal_hits} journal hits)\n  e.g. ${(c.worst_examples || []).slice(0, 3).join(' | ')}`).join('\n')}

For each file:
1. Read it fully.
2. Remove every development-journal fragment, converting the information into mathematics where
   it carries mathematical content (e.g. "STAGE 2 (landed): the map is injective" becomes a
   lemma with a proof) and deleting it otherwise.
3. Any \\begin{proof} that is a sketch: write the real proof, splitting out hard steps as new
   \\label'ed lemma nodes with \\uses edges. Never shrink mathematical content.
4. Keep every \\label, \\lean, \\leanok, \\uses, \\source macro that is correct; fix the ones the
   survey flagged for your files:
   dangling pins: ${JSON.stringify(SURVEY.dangling_pins.filter(p => batch.some(c => p.includes(c.file.split('/').pop().replace('.tex','')))))}
   stub proofs:   ${JSON.stringify(SURVEY.stub_proofs.filter(p => batch.some(c => p.includes(c.file.split('/').pop().replace('.tex','')))))}
5. Do not renumber or rename labels that other chapters \\uses — grep the whole blueprint before
   changing any \\label.
6. Keep lines under 100 characters where practical and avoid constructs that overflow the
   printed margin (long inline math, long \\texttt names): the print build currently reports 734
   overfull boxes.

Return a precise report of what you changed per file, with before/after line counts and the
number of journal fragments removed.`, { label: `clean:${i}`, phase: 'Clean' }),
  (report, batch, i) => agent(`${RULES}
ADVERSARIAL RE-READ. Another agent just rewrote these chapters:
${batch.map(c => '- ' + c.file).join('\n')}

Its report:
${String(report).slice(0, 8000)}

Verify by READING THE FILES AS THEY ARE NOW (do not trust the report):
- Did it delete any mathematical statement, proof, \\label, \\lean, \\leanok, \\uses or \\source
  that should have been kept? Grep the rest of the blueprint for every removed \\label.
- Is any remaining proof still a sketch?
- Is any journal fragment still present (re-grep the full marker list)?
- Did it introduce LaTeX that will not compile (unbalanced braces/environments, undefined macros)?
  Check \\begin/\\end balance mechanically with a python script.
- Did it invent a \\lean{X} for a declaration that does not exist?
FIX what you find yourself (you may edit these chapter files), then report the residual issues.`,
    { label: `check:${i}`, phase: 'Check' }),
)

return { survey: SURVEY, cleaned: cleaned.filter(Boolean).length, batches: BATCHES.length }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remove the elaboration-budget `set_option` scopes a module no longer needs.
#
#   scripts/trim-budgets.sh AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Foo.lean
#
# Mathlib v4.31.0 contains ZERO `set_option maxHeartbeats N in` under Mathlib/ and exactly one
# `synthInstance.maxHeartbeats`.  Every budget here is therefore a deviation that has to earn its
# place.  This script deletes ALL of a module's `maxHeartbeats` / `synthInstance.maxHeartbeats`
# / `maxRecDepth` scope lines at once and re-elaborates the file; if it still elaborates at Lean
# defaults the deletion stands, otherwise the file is restored untouched (then bisect by hand or
# measure the survivors with Mathlib's `count_heartbeats in`).
#
# `lake env lean` is used rather than `lake build`, so the build tree is never invalidated.
# Prints: OK <file> removed <n> | KEEP <file> still needed (<n> scopes) | SKIP <file> none
set -uo pipefail

SRC=${1:?usage: trim-budgets.sh <file.lean>}
OUT=${AJC_DEUMBRELLA_OUT:-/tmp/ajc-minimports}
mkdir -p "$OUT"
base=$(basename "$SRC" .lean)

n=$(grep -cE '^set_option (maxHeartbeats|synthInstance\.maxHeartbeats|maxRecDepth) [0-9]+ in$' "$SRC")
[ "$n" -eq 0 ] && { echo "SKIP  $SRC  no scoped budgets"; exit 0; }

bak="$SRC.budgets.bak"
cp "$SRC" "$bak"
grep -vE '^set_option (maxHeartbeats|synthInstance\.maxHeartbeats|maxRecDepth) [0-9]+ in$' "$bak" > "$SRC"

if lake env lean \
     -Dpp.unicode.fun=true \
     -DrelaxedAutoImplicit=false \
     -DmaxSynthPendingDepth=3 \
     -Dweak.linter.mathlibStandardSet=true \
     "$SRC" > "$OUT/$base.budgets.txt" 2>&1; then
  rm -f "$bak"
  echo "OK    $SRC  removed $n budget scopes"
else
  mv "$bak" "$SRC"
  echo "KEEP  $SRC  $n scopes still needed (see $OUT/$base.budgets.txt)"
fi
